title: api-config-runtime-scratchpad-linda
content:
Context: personal scratchpad for designing the API shape and runtime config contract for the inference API. This is intentionally rough - notes to self, tradeoffs, ASCII diagrams, and open questions.

Goals:
- Minimal surface for customers: single /v1/infer endpoint with extensible config blob.
- Clear separation between user intent (prompt, tools, function-calls) and runtime hints (batching, cache keys, quantization overrides).
- Backward-compatible: allow new runtime hints to be ignored by older servers.

Current thinking (shape):
- top-level: { input, mode, config }
  - input: string | [string] (support single + multi-turn concat)
  - mode: "chat" | "completion" | "embed"
  - config: free-form map of runtime hints (see below)

Runtime-hints proposal (config keys):
- batching: { allow: true|false, max_wait_ms: int, max_batch_tokens: int }
- cache: { key: string, scope: "global"|"customer"|"route", ttl_sec: int }
- quant: { profile: "fp16"|"int8"|"int4", force: true|false }
- fallback_chain: ["gpt-open-8b", "gpt-open-3b"]  // customer-specified fallbacks
- trace_id: string (for tracing across services)
- priority: "low"|"normal"|"high"  // routing hint for smart router

Open questions / tradeoffs:
1) How much of this belongs in the public API vs. entirely in Console/Reserved config? Example: exposing quant.profile to hosted customers may be confusing. Maybe hide detailed quant options behind enterprise flag.
2) cache.key collision surface: should we canonicalize prompt (strip metadata) before hashing? If user passes scope:route, need server-side mapping.
3) Batching max waits: per-tenant or global? We should support per-route overrides via Console.
4) Security: any user-provided key that controls fallback_chain could be used to route to competitor models - enforce allowlist or server-side mapping.

Mini-architecture diagram (text):

Client -> API Gateway -> Request Normalizer -> Router -> Serving Pool(s) -> Model Worker
                      |               |              |-> KV-cache (prefix cache)
                      |               |-> Trace/metrics -> Observability
                      |-> config validation (schema + feature flags)

Notes on validation:
- Use JSON Schema for 'config' with versioned schema (x-config-version). If unknown keys present and x-config-version < N, warn but accept (for forward compatibility).
- Validate batching.cache/quant fields server-side; remap user-friendly aliases (e.g., "fast-low-cost" -> quant.profile=int8+kv).

Compatibility and rollout plan (draft):
- Phase 0: internal alpha - only used by Dedicated/private customers + internal tests. Expose full config.
- Phase 1: beta for Hosted with conservative defaults; hide quant.profile unless enterprise plan. Add allowlist for fallback_chain.
- Phase 2: public GA with Console UI and schema docs.

TODOs (me / next steps):
- [ ] Draft JSON Schema for config (version 1) - TODO: map types and constraints (J. Chen to review)
- [ ] Add example requests/responses for chat streaming with batching enabled
- [ ] Wire up simple server-side canonicalization function for cache.key
- [ ] Discuss security allowlist for fallback models with Security team (ticket INF-142)

Notes-to-self: keep examples small and concrete. Add a short paragraph in the docs about "runtime hints are hints" - not strict guarantees.

Relevant links: Confluence spec draft (linked_artifacts), related PR (#876) - see code for proto changes, Slack thread: #serving-runtime -> search "runtime hints" (Aug-Oct 2025).

Last quick sketch: example request payload:
{
  "input": "Summarize the following...",
  "mode": "completion",
  "config": {
    "batching": {"allow": true, "max_wait_ms": 25},
    "cache": {"key": "sha1:user123:prefix-xyz", "scope": "customer", "ttl_sec": 3600},
    "priority": "normal"
  }
}

End of scratchpad.
